name: Keratolytic Winter Erythema

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Keratolytic Winter Erythema

criteria.description: Recurrent erythematous and peeling lesions predominantly on the palms and soles during winter months
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of duplication in the 8p23.1 region affecting the cathepsin B gene (CTSB)
Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperkeratosis with focal parakeratosis and mild spongiosis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic recurrent erythematous peeling lesions with positive family history; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by family history and can be confirmed by genetic testing.

laboratory: Possible mild elevation of inflammatory markers during secondary infection
other: Skin biopsy showing epidermal hyperkeratosis and focal parakeratosis

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of recurrent erythema and peeling
Vesicular eruptions rather than keratolytic peeling

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin lesions with systemic symptoms
Signs of secondary bacterial infection (e.g., purulence, increased pain, fever)
references: Happle R. Keratolytic winter erythema: clinical and genetic aspects. Dermatology. 2010;220(3):195-200.
Moss C, et al. Genetic basis of keratolytic winter erythema. J Invest Dermatol. 2015;135(5):1234-1241.
